predictions.notes: High-quality franchise (36.6% op margin, 63.2% ROIC, 41.4% FCF margin) at 14.3x earnings and 9.6% FCF yield after a 37% drawdown on AI-disruption fear. Only candidate of four with undistorted growth. Thesis: enterprise core holds and ARR stabilises 8-10%. Thesis-breaker: ARR decays to mid-single digits as Canva/Figma take the prosumer flank.

Best-scoring idea. Asset-light network, 32.8% op margin, 9.09B FCF, share count -20.7%. But priced at 25x earnings with guidance decelerating to 4-6%, negative equity from buybacks, and 55 insider sells vs 0 buys. Headline 31.7% revenue CAGR is a covid-trough artefact; real recent rate ~16%.

AVOID at 67.6. Quality operator, 12.5% FCF yield fully returned to holders, D/E 0.27. But revenue has fallen three straight years (-6,-2,-4%) and the 15.5% CAGR is a 2020 oil-crash artefact. Return depends chiefly on the oil price, which I cannot forecast. Logged to test calibration on a rejected idea.

latestReview.assumptionsHeld: Nothing about the business analysis has been contradicted: revenue had fallen three consecutive years and the 15.5pct headline CAGR was a 2020 oil-crash artefact. Both still true.
latestReview.assumptionsBroken: The AVOID rating as a price prediction. Up 12.2pct, within 2.4pct of my 167 target. And the REASON is the thing I named: I rejected it saying the return depends chiefly on the oil price which I cannot forecast - and Brent moved above 100 USD on Middle East tension. I was right that oil would decide it, then treated my own inability to forecast oil as a reason to expect a poor outcome.

predictions.notes: AVOID at 66.2, weakest of four. Operating income fell three straight years (1.68-1.56-1.53B) while revenue grew 10%; flat EPS is manufactured by a 20.5% share-count reduction, not by earning more. Only +1.6% probability-weighted return at 20.4x earnings with no valuation cushion.

latestReview.assumptionsHeld: Nothing yet. The concern that drove the AVOID - operating income falling three straight years while revenue grew, with flat EPS manufactured by a 20.5pct share-count reduction - has not been tested. Ulta has not reported since; next results are due around 3 December 2026.
latestReview.assumptionsBroken: The AVOID rating itself, as a prediction about the SHARE PRICE. Up 13.7pct and past my 615 target. But note precisely what did and did not happen: the stock re-rated on no new information about the margin problem. My analysis is not yet shown to be wrong - it is shown to be slow.

predictions.notes: Strongest idea of the session. Only candidate with revenue, operating income AND net income rising every year for five years (rev 12.73->21.45B, NI 2.07->4.57B), no base-year distortion. 18.3x earnings, 10.4pct FCF yield on 8.66B FCF, 40.4pct FCF margin. Reverse DCF implies the price assumes FCF SHRINKS 5.9pct/yr vs 22.1pct delivered. Down 38pct YTD on AI-disruption fear. Thesis-breaker: QuickBooks retention slipping, not just TurboTax pricing.

High quality operator riding an AI capex boom - which is the problem. IT datacom is 43pct of sales and grew 89pct YoY; Q3 guided to 50-52pct growth. Trailing 23.2x sits on peak-cycle earnings. Worst bear case of the five at -38pct. Logged as WATCH not BUY precisely because my own lessons warn against buying a cyclical at a full multiple on boom-year trailing figures.

Best-measured company in the screen (16/16 scoring components). CAD/PLM switching costs are punitive - migrating an engineering record means re-validating decades of product data. ARR 2.448B growing 9.1pct cc beat guidance; FY26 guide raised to 9-9.5pct. Op margin 35.9pct, FCF 857M, cash conversion 1.18x, profit jump organic not divestiture-driven. Ceiling is low: a 9pct grower does not re-rate hard.

Best-dated catalyst in the screen: zanzalintinib NDA under FDA review with target action date 3 December 2026, and 2026 guidance of 2.53-2.63B explicitly EXCLUDES it. Op income 0.29->0.87B, 37.6pct op margin, shares -11.4pct. But binary: essentially all revenue is cabozantinib, which peaks ~2.8B by 2029 before generic erosion. A large part of this outcome resolves on one regulatory date.

Cleanest compounding record of the five (rev 3.58->5.65B, NI 0.78->1.52B, all five years) at 33.4pct op margin and 25.9pct ROIC. But the nearest dated catalyst is NEGATIVE: Astral ventilator suspension costs 75M revenue and 0.15 EPS in FY2027. Structural bear case is real - Lilly GLP-1 approved for sleep apnea WITHOUT CPAP, and Philips re-entering the US market it vacated. Lowest score of the five.

latestReview.assumptionsHeld: The compounding record was real - revenue, operating income and net income all rose five straight years, 33.4pct op margin, 25.9pct ROIC, flat share count. The business quality judgement was correct.
latestReview.assumptionsBroken: My target of 252 was reached in 42 days on a 12-month thesis. I scored catalysts 4/10 - the lowest of that session - on the grounds that the nearest dated catalyst was NEGATIVE (the Astral suspension) and that the GLP-1 overhang would keep the multiple constrained. The multiple expanded anyway. My range was -28pct to +31pct against 28.4pct annualised volatility: barely one sigma.

predictions.notes: Only new idea clearing 70 this session. Revenue, operating income and net income all rose every year (rev 1.49-2.86B, op 0.25-0.62B, NI 0.15-0.48B); Q1 2026 product sales 811M +44pct YoY. Two commercial products - INGREZZA plus CRENESSITY, which holds an effective monopoly in CAH. Reverse DCF implies 12.7pct FCF growth vs 28.0pct delivered. Thesis-breaker: INGREZZA pricing pressure, since it still carries most of revenue. Share count ROSE 4.8pct - no buyback offsetting comp.

Only new idea clearing 70 this session. 10.4x earnings, 11.0pct FCF yield, 16.2pct ROIC, 15/16 data coverage. Reverse DCF implies FCF SHRINKS 8.9pct/yr vs +8.9pct delivered - market prices permanent decline. BUT management CUT operating margin guidance from 31pct to 25-26pct on AI investment after the Cognigy deal, and faces Microsoft plus Salesforce entering CX directly. THIRD instance of the same bet as ADBE and INTU - do not hold all three. Thesis-breaker: AI agents displacing per-seat pricing.

summary.note: Report all three together. One takeover once made the book look 3 points ahead of the index when, excluding it, it was 1.6 points behind.
